html:
The Yanesha, once called Amuesha, are an Arawakan-speaking people of the central Peruvian rainforest, in the valleys of the Palcazu, Pichis and Chanchamayo rivers on the eastern slopes of the Andes. Their land lies where the highlands meet the Amazon, and for centuries they traded salt and forest goods with Andean peoples.

Franciscan missions entered their valleys in the 1600s and 1700s. In 1742 many Yanesha joined the great rebellion of Juan Santos Atahualpa, which drove the missions out of the central forest for about a hundred years. In the 1800s coffee planters and European colonists, such as the German settlers of Pozuzo and Oxapampa, took much of their best land. Their neighbours include the Asháninka. See Peru.
